summary: A target-level plan for relative endoscopy on the infinitesimal unitary Friedberg–Jacquet symmetric space, culminating in Leslie’s all-residue-characteristic unramified unit fundamental lemma. It imports ordinary endoscopy, local Hermitian forms and densities, quotient measures and spherical Levi descent. The local-to-spherical reduction is specified without assuming relative transfer in the independent Jacquet–Rallis spectral input. All six stages have targets; unresolved analytic, normalization, sibling-export and conjectural inputs are explicit, so this complete pass does not claim closure.

nodes.title: The off-diagonal unitary representation
nodes.statement: For nondegenerate Hermitian E-spaces W1,W2 of the same dimension n, put W=W1 orthogonal-sum W2 and theta=Ad(1,-1). Identify the (-1)-eigenspace in Lie U(W) with Hom_E(W2,W1) by X mapping to the block matrix [[0,X],[-X^tau,0]], where h1(Xv,w)=h2(v,X^tau w). Its fixed-group action is (g1,g2).X=g1 X g2^(-1).
hypotheses: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero; E/F is a quadratic field extension.
Hermitian forms are conjugate-linear in the first variable and linear in the second.
proofSteps: Use the adjoint anti-involution imported from GN.2 and solve the skew-adjoint block equations.
Transport the fixed-group conjugation action through the block identification.
acceptance: The block has zero diagonal blocks and its lower-left block is minus the adjoint.

nodes.title: The two signed contractions

Both are F-polynomial maps. r1 is equivariant for U(W1) and invariant under U(W2); r2 has the opposite equivariance. In standard Gram coordinates the formulas use Matrix.conjTranspose, not plain transpose.

Hermitian forms are conjugate-linear in the first variable and linear in the second.

Use adjoint_action to verify the two transformation laws.

nodes.title: Invariant quotients of the symmetric representation
nodes.statement: The morphism r1 realizes Hom_E(W2,W1)//U(W2) as Herm(W1), equivariantly for U(W1). Taking the quotient by both unitary groups gives affine n-space: the quotient map is the n nonleading coefficients of charpoly(r1(X)). These are categorical quotients of F-varieties, not assertions that every F-point has a preimage.

Use the split multiplication-map section and its generic transitive fibers in Igusa’s criterion (supplier request SF.1).

Import the GL_n characteristic-coefficient invariant quotient from ET.2b/chevalley-quotient and transport it along multiplication by a trace-zero scalar between the Hermitian and skew-Hermitian representations. Descend the coordinate-algebra identifications with SF.1/galois-descent-affine.

nodes.title: Regular semisimplicity excludes singular Hom maps
nodes.statement: For the symmetric representation, regular semisimple means a closed geometric orbit of maximal dimension. An element X is regular semisimple exactly when r1(X) is an invertible regular semisimple Hermitian endomorphism. In particular X is invertible and the stabilizer in U(W1) times U(W2) is a rank-n torus. The off-diagonal block has characteristic polynomial charpoly(r1(X))(T^2).
hypotheses: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero; E/F is a quadratic field extension.
Hermitian forms are conjugate-linear in the first variable and linear in the second.
proofSteps: In split coordinates identify closed regular orbits with separable nonzero eigenvalues of the product.
Compute the block characteristic polynomial by a Schur-complement identity; a zero product eigenvalue produces a repeated zero block root.
Descend the criterion and use the centralizer description from ET.0.
acceptance: The zero map fails regular semisimplicity for n>0.
A diagonal X with distinct nonzero norm squares yields a regular example.

nodes.title: The contraction torsor and rational-class kernels
nodes.statement: On invertible Hom maps, r1 is a U(W2)-torsor as a morphism of F-varieties over Herm(W1)^invertible. On F-points its image is the open-and-closed norm-form component Omega(W1,W2); no rational surjectivity onto all invertible Hermitian endomorphisms is asserted. At X, projection (g1,g2) to g1 identifies H_X with T_r1(X); its inverse sends t to (t,X^(-1)tX). For regular semisimple X it induces D(H_X,U(W1) times U(W2);F) isomorphic to D(T_r1(X),U(W1);F), compatibly with inv and the rational orbits inside a stable class.
hypotheses: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero; E/F is a quadratic field extension.
Hermitian forms are conjugate-linear in the first variable and linear in the second.
proofSteps: Check the geometric fibers are free transitive right U(W2)-orbits, then descend the torsor.
Solve tX=Xg2 to obtain the inverse stabilizer map.
Use the determinant description of unitary H1 to identify the two kernel conditions; the two component obstruction maps agree on H1(H_X).
acceptance: For n=1 the F-point image is one norm coset, although the geometric torsor is surjective.
The induced map preserves the neutral rational orbit.

Obtain convergence from the closed regular orbit and compact support; transport the regular-orbit measure, as requested from ET.1.

nodes.title: Orbital pushforward along contraction
nodes.statement: For T=r1(X) in Omega(W1,W2), set r_!f(T)=integral over U(W2) of f(Xu) du. It is independent of X and is zero off Omega in the invertible Hermitian locus. For f supported compactly in the invertible Hom locus, r_!f is a compactly supported locally constant function on that locus. For arbitrary f on all Hom maps it is only locally constant on the invertible locus with relatively compact support in the ambient Hermitian space; it need not be compactly supported within the invertible locus. The map on compact nonsingular tests is onto C_c^infinity(Omega).

nodes.title: Relative endoscopic data and symmetric spaces
nodes.statement: For n=a+b with a,b positive, a relative datum Xi consists of an ordinary elliptic endoscopic datum (U(Va) times U(Vb),s,xi) for U(W1), together with Hermitian forms alpha on E^a and beta on E^b. Its symmetric representation is Hom_E(V_alpha,Va) direct-sum Hom_E(V_beta,Vb), with acting group (U(Va) times U(V_alpha)) times (U(Vb) times U(V_beta)). The reference spaces Va,Vb and the varying spaces V_alpha,V_beta are retained separately even if their unitary groups happen to be isomorphic.

Hermitian forms are conjugate-linear in the first variable and linear in the second.
proofSteps: Import the ordinary datum and local Hermitian isometry classes.
Apply symmetric-representation separately in ranks a and b; use the product contraction r_alpha,beta.
acceptance: For a=b=1 there are four pairs of Hermitian isometry classes, with the same ordinary endoscopic group.

nodes.statement: Regular semisimple delta and (delta_a,delta_b) match for Xi exactly when r1(delta) and (r1(delta_a),r1(delta_b)) match under the ordinary Hermitian endoscopic relation. Hermitian forms are conjugate-linear in the first variable and linear in the second.

Pull back the factor along the pair of contractions and the character along torsor.
For nicely matching contractions the reference factor is eta(resultant)*absolute-value(resultant), with the ET.1 inv correction otherwise.

routeRecords.title: Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison, Part II: relative endoscopy for unitary symmetric spaces and the unitary Friedberg–Jacquet fundamental lemma
routeRecords.brief:
Part II of Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison). It starts where ET.0–ET.3 stop: those layers plan stable conjugacy, endoscopic data, transfer factors, κ-orbital integrals, the fundamental lemma and transfer for unitary groups and their Lie algebras. This Part II develops endoscopy for the symmetric space U(W_1 ⊕ W_2)/U(W_1) × U(W_2) at the infinitesimal level, whose relative trace formula governs the unitary Friedberg–Jacquet periods ∫_{[U(W_1)×U(W_2)]}φ and is not stable, and proves its fundamental lemma. Source: Spencer Leslie, 'The endoscopic fundamental lemma for unitary Friedberg–Jacquet periods' (Ann. of Math. 201 (2025), 551–645; arXiv:1911.07907), Part 1 and §11.2.

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 2.12 (= Theorem 1.3): for E/F an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic zero, V_n = W_1 = W_2 split with self-dual lattice Λ_n = Λ_a ⊕ Λ_b, and an elliptic relative endoscopic datum Ξ = (U(V_a) × U(V_b), s, ξ, α, β): if (α, β) = (I_a, I_b), 1_{End(Λ_n)} and 1_{End(Λ_a)} ⊗ 1_{End(Λ_b)} match; otherwise 1_{End(Λ_n)} matches 0. Theorem 3.5 (= Proposition 1.5): for every φ in the spherical Hecke algebra of GL_n(E), φ ∗ 1_0 and ξ_(a,b)(φ) ∗ 1_0 are endoscopic smooth transfers on Herm(V_n). Proposition 1.6: {(φ ∗ 1_0) ⊗ 1_{Λ_n}, 0} and BC(φ) ⊗ 1_{L_n} are Jacquet–Rallis transfers in the sense of (4.3). Theorem 5.3 (= Theorem 1.7): for X ∈ GL_n(F)^rss, ω(X) Orb^{GL_{n−1}(F),η}(BC(φ), X) = Orb^{U(V_{n−1})}(φ ∗ 1_0, Y) if X matches Y ∈ X_n^rss, and 0 otherwise.

Cover: (1) the infinitesimal symmetric pair (U(W_1) × U(W_2), 𝔲(W)_1 = Hom_E(W_2, W_1)), its regular semisimple locus, the contraction maps r_i, the categorical quotients (Proposition 2.1, Lemma 2.2, by Igusa's criterion), the torsor Lemma 2.3 with D(H_δ/F) ≅ D(T_{r(δ)}/F), relative orbital integrals, the pushforward r_! and Lemma 2.5; (2) relative endoscopic data Ξ, endoscopic symmetric pairs, matching, Δ_rel = Δ(r_{α,β}(−), r(−)), RO^κ, SRO and relative smooth transfer (Definition 2.10), with the existence of transfers ([Les19, Conjecture 4.4]) and Remark 2.11 (independence of the contraction) as stated targets, not proved; (3) the Hermitian symmetric variety X_n, its spherical Hecke module with Hironaka's theorems (freeness of rank 2^n; the spherical Fourier transform H with H(φ ∗ 1_0) = BC(φ)), the Hecke morphism ξ_(a,b) through non-tempered normalized induction, and Lemmas 3.1–3.2; (4) the initial reduction (Φ^n = r_!1_{End(Λ_n)}, Lemma 3.8, Corollary 3.10, Lemma 3.11, Proposition 3.12); (5) Xiao's germ expansion (Proposition 4.5, Lemma 4.6, Theorem 4.7), his construction of endoscopic transfer through Jacquet–Rallis transfer and Lie-algebraic parabolic descent (Xiao, Theorem 6.1), and Proposition 4.8; (6) the Weil-representation reduction (Proposition 5.2) and Proposition 1.6; (7) the deduction of Theorem 5.3 from the base change fundamental lemma (Theorem 11.1) in §11.2. Remark 3.7's extension of ξ_(a,b) to all of ℋ(X_n), with augmented transfer factors, is a separate open target.

Import, never re-plan: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.0 (stable conjugacy, endoscopic data, Kottwitz–Borovoi cohomology; Lemma 1.8 and Lemma 2.7 are routed there), ET.1 (Langlands–Shelstad–Kottwitz transfer factors, κ-orbital integrals, matching functions; the simplified unitary factor (2.7) is routed there) and ET.3 (existence of endoscopic transfer on Herm, Theorem 2.9); the pending Part II JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (Lie-algebra Jacquet–Rallis matching, transfers (4.3) and (4.7), Zhang's existence theorem, the Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma, the Weil representation on orbital integrals, and the base change fundamental lemma Theorem 11.1); SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (Satake; Macdonald's formula, Hall–Littlewood branching and parabolic descent versus Levi restriction are routed there); GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2–GN.3 (Hermitian spaces and lattices, Jacobowitz's K_{n,E}-orbits on X_n, representation densities); AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2 (measures). Prerequisites: Leslie [Les19], [Les22], [Les24]; Xiao [Xia18]; Hironaka [Hir99]; Getz–Wambach for Conjecture 1.1. Tests: n = 2, a = b = 1 (computed in [Les19]); Φ^n_d = 0 for odd d and Φ^n_{2d} = Σ_{λ∈P^+_{n,2d}} m_0(ϖ^λ)1_λ with m_0 a representation density; ξ̂_(a,b)(Sat(1_d)) = Σ Sat(1_{d_a} ⊗ 1_{d_b}).

This route coalesces with JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison, proposed by PAPER-ZHANG-21 and extended by PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21, PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 and PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-25; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. Leslie, 'The endoscopic fundamental lemma for unitary Friedberg–Jacquet periods' (Ann. of Math. 201 (2025), 551–645), §§4.1, 5.1 and Part 2, adds a twisted Jacquet–Rallis comparison that switches the roles of the rational linear group and the unitary group: G′ = Res_{E/F}(GL_n × GL_{n+1}) with H′ = Res_{E/F}GL_n on one side and H′_{x,y} = U(V_x) × U(V_y) on the other, for all pairs of Hermitian forms, against G = GL_n × GL_{n+1} with H = GL_n on both sides and the character η(det h_2).

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 11.1: for E/F an unramified extension of p-adic local fields and φ in the spherical Hecke algebra of G′(F), BC(φ) matches {φ at (w_n, w_{n+1}), 0 elsewhere}: Ω(γ) Orb^η(BC(φ), γ) = Orb(φ, δ) for γ ↔^{w_n,w_{n+1}} δ, and Orb^η(BC(φ), γ) = 0 when γ matches an orbit for (x, y) outside the G′(F)-orbit of (w_n, w_{n+1}). Theorem 9.11: for E/F with every archimedean place split, (x, y) fixed, a cuspidal Π ≅ Π^σ of G′(𝔸_F) with Π_{v_0} ≅ π_0 ⊗ π_0 supercuspidal at a split place, and an ω′-nice f′ that is essentially a matrix coefficient at v_0, there is an ω-nice matching f with (1/L(1, η)²) J^{x,y}_Π(f′) = Σ_{π∈B(Π)} I_π(f), and f can be chosen with ∏_v J^{x,y,♮}_{Π_v}(f′_v) = ∏_v I^♮_{π_v}(f_v).

Add, after the candidate's Lie-algebra layers (the paper restates their statements: the matching (4.2), transfers (4.3) and (4.7), Zhang's existence Theorem 4.2, the fundamental lemma Theorem 4.3 and Beuzart-Plessis's Weil representation on orbital integrals, Proposition 5.1): (1) the group-level twisted set-up (w_n, θ, σ, quasi-split V_n), the orbit matching of Lemmas 7.1–7.2 and Proposition 7.3, invariant polynomials, orbital integrals (7.5)–(7.7) and the transfer factor Ω(γ) = ω(γ_1^{-1}γ_2); (2) Z-regular semisimple elements and the non-surjective norm on centers (Lemma 7.5, Remark 7.6, Lemma 7.7) with orbital integrals over Nm(Z_{G′}); (3) local transfer (Proposition 7.8 in the split case, Theorem 7.9, Corollary 7.10, Lemma 7.11) and the unit fundamental lemma Theorem 7.12; (4) global distributions: the Petersson factorization, unitary periods P_x with the Feigon–Lapid–Offen local functionals (Theorem 8.5, Lemma 8.6) and P_x(φ) = 2L(1, π × π^∨ · η)∏_v α^♮_x(W_v) (Proposition 8.7), Jacquet's distinction theorems [Jac05], [Jac10], global and normalized local relative characters I_π, J^{x,y}_Π and their factorizations (8.13), (8.14); (5) the simple relative trace formulas for nice test functions (Lemmas 9.3–9.4, Propositions 9.5–9.6), global matching (9.3), efficient transfers, Proposition 9.9 and Theorem 9.11; (6) local spectral results: Lemma 10.1 (Sakellaridis–Venkatesh for strongly tempered pairs and Ichino–Zhang's Appendix A of [Zha14b]), the split identity Proposition 10.4, the unramified identity Lemma 10.6, the weak transfer Proposition 10.7 and Corollary 10.8; (7) the globalization proof of Theorem 11.1 (Lemmas 11.2, 11.3, 11.5 and Proposition 11.4). The consumer is the proposed UnitaryFriedbergJacquetRelativeEndoscopy (Theorem 5.3 through §11.2).

Construct the fixed-α partially linearized RTF, its regular-orbit absolute/local uniform convergence, nilpotent Tate regularization, rank-one and CM-field reduction, and entire SL2-automorphic J_s. Use Mihatsch–Zhang DOI10.4171/JEMS/1375 §7.2's corrected Gaussians; repair the Weyl/sign descent in §12.4 before treating Lemma12.6 as proved. Do not assert full archimedean Gaussian-transfer existence, which this paper only expects. Endpoints: Theorem12.14 entire modularity; Proposition13.3 holomorphic coherent weight-n series; Theorem13.4 conditional comparison; Theorem13.9 group/semi-Lie FL for unramified quadratic p-adic fields with odd residue characteristic and q≥n. The FL extends to all relative regular orbits by density; the arithmetic consumer's AFL does not thereby extend. Include the exact residue-cardinality bound and all group/semi-Lie rank shifts. Tests: n=1 corrected Bessel integral and derivative; transfer scaling by η(a)^n; n=2 Weyl-fibre counterexample and repaired descent; norm-unit lower-rank reduction; product of rational transfer factors1. This analytic owner has no dependence on RZ spaces or the AFL, preventing circular proof of its FL input.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21), to respect when stating the layers:
- Proposition 4.12(i) and Proposition 2.7(i) at q = n: the printed proof picks ξ ∈ F¹ with det(1 − ξg′) a unit, but it also needs 1 − ξd to be a unit, which can fail for every admissible ξ when q = n (FL counterexample with q = n = 3). So the reduction '(b) for V_{n−1} ⇒ (a) for V_n' is proved only for q ≥ n + 1. Plan the q = n case separately: for the FL it is covered by Beuzart-Plessis's independent proof; for the AFL at p = n (Theorem 15.1(a)) the printed argument leaves a gap.
- Theorem 5.5 (local constancy) is proved as printed only for q ≥ n; cite Mihatsch (Algebra Number Theory 16 (2022)) in general.
- Lemma 4.3(iii) and Lemma 4.9(iii) need det(1 − g) ≠ 0, and Lemma 4.10's 'srs' holds only for all but finitely many ξ.
- The Gaussian test functions of §12 must use Mihatsch–Zhang's corrected normalisation (E12): for ψ(x) = e^{2πix}, (12.4), Lemmas 12.5 and 12.11 and 'φ̂ = φ' are false as printed; (8.11) needs 4π, not 2π.
- §11.4 and §12.5 use opposite sign conventions for the action on V′, so the regular and nilpotent derivatives in (12.38) must be normalised consistently; Lemma 12.6 omits the archimedean transfer-factor phase for n ≥ 2.
- Propositions 2.7(ii) and 4.12(ii) are applied in §13 at places where their printed q-bound fails; their proofs do not use the bound, so state them without it.

routeRecords.title: Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison, Part II: rigid inner forms and real tempered packets
routeRecords.brief:
Build on Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison), with its ET.0 ordinary stable-conjugacy, nonabelian/abelianized H1 and torus-complex Tate–Nakayama package as the first prerequisite. Import ET.1 transfer factors and their explicit conventions, and the real distribution characters ET.1 builds from AF.1 (P18), Arithmetic Galois duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1,R02.2,D7), the existing Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology and ClassFieldTheory roadmaps, ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a/RG2.5, Automorphic forms (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1) and Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0/SR.2/SR.3). Use the pinned continuous cochain, low Tate degree, Kummer, abstract extension and algebraic torus carriers. Do not reconstruct them or treat them as the missing continuous comparisons.

Construct u as the inverse limit of Res mu_n/diagonal mu_n over characteristic-zero local F, prove H1(F,u)=0 and H2(F,u)=Zhat for p-adic F or C2 for R, choose xi=-1 and realize the profinite extension W. Keep W distinct from W_F and use discrete G(Fbar) in its cocycles. Define affine central-pair categories, algebraic central restrictions, barred cocycles and rigid H1 with their exact functorialities. Use the author’s direct proof to lift H1(F,G/Z) for arbitrary affine, including disconnected, G. Prove finite fixed-Z classes and all reductive inner forms rigidify. Define abelianized rigid H1 using the simply connected cover of the TWISTED group, not only untwisted H1 vanishing.

Construct Ybar/IY, the reductive coroot quotient and their norm-kernel colimit. Import the generic unbalanced cochain operation from ArithmeticGaloisDuality, choose Weil lifts before coset representatives, and extend finite maps to quotient tori before root-extracted cochain evaluation. Prove the explicit torus isomorphism Theorem4.8 and reductive H1_ab isomorphism Theorem4.11 with the normalized restriction squares. Prove the dual plus-component pairing: trivial left kernel on H1_ab, perfect for p-adic F or tori, real norm-annihilator image in general. Define rigid groupoids, stable-conjugacy and torus-embedding invariants with eta^-1 transport, and prove the all-Z strong-real-form equivalence Theorem5.2. Fixed-Z fibers are finite; the all-Z union only MAY be infinite.

Define refined endoscopic data and parameter-centralizer covers here. This Part II also owns the rigid transfer factors: the normalized absolute factor (5.1), the relative comparison tori of §5.1, the independence and invariance of Proposition 5.6, and the prime convention (5.10). Build them on ET.1's ordinary factors, Whittaker normalization and ordinary product formula, which it imports and does not extend. Construct the real Weil carrier once, importing ordinary archimedean reciprocity. Cover the full real tempered case beyond ET.1’s unitary application range: Langlands discrete-series parameters, admissible embeddings, Whittaker normalization, minimal cuspidal Levi, R-group root subsystem, positive-root Cayley transforms, coherent continuation, the noncompact imaginary-root criterion and irreducible induction. Correct both printed Cayley formulas using Shelstad1982 p423. Prove Theorem5.8, the parity image, Proposition5.9’s exact component sequence, the full real compound-packet bijection and stable characters, then Proposition5.10 and identity(5.11) with the prime transfer convention. Real component groups are abelian here but may have order4 elements; p-adic lifted groups may be nonabelian. This Part II is the single supplier of the rigid objects for PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22's proposed HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukasKottwitzPartII, whose items 008–010 consume D06 (rigid H1), T13 (Corollary 3.8), T44 (the Corollary 5.4 pairing, on H1_ab as the author's erratum E05 corrects it), D27 and D35 (Z(Gbar_hat)^+ and S_phi^+) and C01/C02 (the refined local Langlands conjecture and its character identities). State them for real and p-adic F. The refined correspondence stays a conjecture for p-adic F. HKW's p-adic application adapters, including item 010's inverse-limit universal-cover interface, stay in that Part II.

Final proved local endpoints are the finite/dual rigid cohomology theorems, equivalence with strong real forms, and the real tempered labeling, stability and endoscopic identities. The general p-adic refined LLC is only a conjecture specification. Include the SL2 example with Q8 labels and dimension2 weighting using its actual representation-theoretic supplier. Add a later global interface from Kal15b, explicitly restricted to the overview’s number-field/quasi-split/simply-connected-derived assumptions: global gerbe, localization modulo central coboundaries, global duality and rigid lift. Prove here, from ET.1's ordinary product formula, the unconditional adelic product of rigid transfer factors and the mediating functions for Arthur's globalization hypothesis (§5.7, via Kal15b Proposition 4.1). The adelic packet/pairing is conditional on local packet conjectures and the conjectural global Langlands group; Conjecture5.11 is not a proved multiplicity formula.

Tests must include mu_n in the real norm-one torus giving C_(2n), split-torus vanishing, the two compact SL2 rigid labels with equal abelianization, a disconnected finite central cocycle lift, odd-order inverse/positive transfer signs, Q8’s four one-dimensional and one two-dimensional labels, a real C4 component group, an irrelevant packet, a vanishing coherent continuation and the corrected rank-one Cayley product. routeRecords.title: Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison, Part II: geometric stabilisation via p-adic integration
routeRecords.brief: Build the second proof of Ngô's Geometric Stabilisation Theorem, the one that replaces the Decomposition and Support Theorems by p-adic integration on coarse moduli spaces of Deligne–Mumford stacks. The final theorems are those of Groechenig–Wyss–Ziegler: (1) Geometric Stabilisation (their Theorem 1.1 = Corollary 6.18, Ngô's Theorem 6.4.2): for k a finite field with q elements, X/k a smooth projective curve with a rational point ∞, G/X a quasi-split reductive group scheme with |Θ ⋉ W| invertible, D of even degree d ≥ 2g − 2 with A^♦ ≠ ∅, and a coendoscopic datum E = (κ, ρ_κ, ρ_κ → ρ) for Ĝ whose torsor ρ_{κ,∞} splits, one has #^{κ_a} M̄_{G,a}(k) = q^{r^G_H(D)} #^stab M̄_{H,a}(k) for every a ∈ Ã_H(k), where r^G_H(D) = ½(dim M̃_G − dim M̃_H); (2) the geometric non-standard fundamental lemma (their Theorem 1.3 = Corollary 6.17, Ngô's Theorem 8.8.2): #^stab M̃_{G,a}(k) = #^stab M̃_{Ĝ,a}(k) for every a ∈ Ã_G(k) ≅ Ã_Ĝ(k). The roadmap must cover, in this order: p-adic integration of top-degree forms on F-analytic manifolds and Weil's point-count formula; the canonical measure vol_M on the coarse moduli space of a smooth tame Deligne–Mumford stack which is Zariski-locally a finite étale quotient, with the gauge forms its construction needs; twisted inertia stacks, the specialisation map e : M(O_F)^♮ → [I_µ̂M(k)], the weight function and the volume formula vol_M(e^{-1}(x, α)) = q^{-w(x,α)}/|Aut(x, α)| (their Theorem 2.21); torsors over local fields, the stacks X_{Γ,Q}, and the identification of the Hasse invariant with the invariant of a gerbe on the twisted inertia stack (their Proposition 3.7 and Corollary 3.14); quasi-split reductive group schemes over a curve, their outer forms and Langlands duals, the abstract Prym as W-equivariant T-torsors with +-structure, Beilinson 1-motives, and duality of the Pryms of G and Ĝ in the quasi-split case, proved by co-descent and norm maps for étale sheaves (their Appendix A); coendoscopic data and the description of the twisted inertia stack of the anisotropic Higgs stack and of its rigidification by them (their Theorems 5.14 and 5.23); and finally the comparison of the two p-adic integrals, the resulting character-sum identity (their Theorem 6.11), the Fourier inversion over the component group of the Prym, and the Tate-duality argument for Hitchin fibres of Section 6.5. Import, and do not re-plan: the Hitchin system itself — Chevalley quotient, Kostant section, regular centralisers, the stack of G-Higgs bundles, the Hitchin base and map, cameral covers, the Picard stack and its component groups, and the anisotropic locus — from Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison), stage ET.2b, whose sheaf-theoretic route (weak abelian fibrations, δ-stratification, the support theorem) this roadmap deliberately does not use; the deduction of the fundamental lemma from geometric stabilisation, and Waldspurger's non-standard variant, from ET.3 of the same roadmap; endoscopic data and endoscopy groups from ET.0; algebraic stacks, coarse spaces and rigidification from Algebraic moduli for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry), stages R09.4 and R09.5; p-adic measures and integration from Logic and definability in number theory (LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory), stage LD.2; the local invariant map and the Brauer group of a local field from the Tau Ceti roadmap Class field theory, Layer 5; Hilbert 90 and the Galois interface from the Tau Ceti roadmap Profinite cohomology, Layer 9; local duality for abelian varieties from Arithmetic Galois duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality), stage R02.4; pinned reductive group schemes and their automorphisms from the Tau Ceti roadmap Reductive groups, Layers 7 and 9; and the pinned dual group from Geometric Satake and fusion (GeometricSatakeAndFusion), stage GS4:integral-dual-group. State separately, as its own layer, the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula for Deligne–Mumford stacks over a finite field ([Sun12]), which no roadmap owns and which every point count in the proof presupposes.
routeRecords.reason: The atlas already aims at exactly these two theorems: ET.2b plans the endoscopic comparison of κ-isotypic perverse direct images along Ngô's route, and ET.3 derives the ordinary and non-standard fundamental lemma from it. What this paper adds is a second, independent proof of the same statements which avoids the Decomposition and Support Theorems that ET.2a and ET.2b rest on, and it needs machinery that no layer of the atlas plans: p-adic integration on coarse moduli of tame Deligne–Mumford stacks, twisted inertia stacks and the specialisation map, gerbes and the Hasse invariant, coendoscopic data and the endoscopic description of the twisted inertia stack of the Higgs stack, and duality of Pryms for quasi-split group schemes. That is new layers in the direction of an existing roadmap, so it is a Part II rather than a new roadmap; it imports the Hitchin system from ET.2b instead of planning it a second time.
